source.title: Normalization Before Shaking Toward Learning Symmetrically Distributed Representation Without Margin in Speech Emotion Recognition

record.file_problem: Full text present; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The study experimentally varies shaking, batch-normalization layout, and batch-normalization initialization, then reports training–validation accuracy gaps. These are related measurements of generalization, but none of the claim’s eight versions names these interventions or the speech-emotion setting.
record.gate_note: Results on MNIST and CIFAR-10 include test accuracies and errors, but do not test the listed claim versions. Prior-work results quoted in Table 1 are not recorded as this study’s results. The speech-emotion experiments report validation UA and training–validation UA gap; the gap rows are included below. Fixed batch size and dropout probability are setup details, not tested conditions.
record.test_reason: The study uses dropout as a fixed regularizer but tests shaking and batch-normalization design, which no listed version names. It does not compare dropout settings or report results testing V1–V8.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is broadly accurate, but the proposed representation mechanism should be described as the authors' interpretation of embedding analyses. They conclude that directly preceding batch normalization preserves dispersed, approximately symmetric representations during shaking, and that smaller gamma initialization can significantly reduce speech-emotion training–validation gaps while maintaining or improving validation accuracy.
record.recipe_differences: Tests Shake-Shake regularization and batch-normalization layout or initialization in speech-emotion recognition; it does not test random-label memorization, width, optimizer comparisons, batch-size effects, dropout effects, sharpness measures, or memorized-example removal.
record.method_sensitivity: The measured gap changes with residual-block layout, shaking granularity, and batch-normalization γ initialization.

fits_no_version.finding: Speech-emotion training–validation accuracy gaps depend on shaking, residual-block layout, and batch-normalization initialization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In this speech-emotion setup, suitably initialized batch normalization with shaking can significantly reduce the training–validation gap while improving validation accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: MNIST and CIFAR-10 ablations show that shaking performance depends on directly preceding batch normalization. MNIST test accuracy changes from 98.28% to 93.22% with shaking in PreAct, versus 98.66% to 98.90% in PreActBN. CIFAR-10 errors are 2.95%, 3.65%, and 6.92% for shaken PreActBN, BN-Shake, and PreAct.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Batch-normalization placement strongly affects the held-out performance of Shake-Shake convolutional networks.

record.problems: Speech-emotion results use six aggregated corpora and four-fold actor-set cross-validation; experiments are run three times. The text reports p-values for selected comparisons, but does not give uncertainty intervals for all table entries. The MNIST/CIFAR-10 ablations do not report generalization-gap values in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted from the reported speech-emotion generalization-gap results in Tables 2, 6, 8 and 10. Table 1 contains cited prior-work results and is not recorded as this study’s own result.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its comparison with natural-label training and held-out accuracy.
Width sweeps beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer comparisons and tuning-dependent generalization.
Batch-size comparisons and recipe adaptations under controlled training budgets.
Dropout addition, removal, strength, training-set-size dependence, and interaction with augmentation or weight decay. Dropout remains fixed at 0.5 in the speech experiments.
Magnitude-scaled weight perturbations, their association with generalization gaps, and comparisons with other measures.
Identifying memorized examples and comparing their removal with random removal.

record.verdict_notes: All row states are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8 because none measures a listed version. Table 1 is not entirely cited prior work: its PreActBN, BN-Shake, and PreAct results are this study's own experiments. Their omission does not create a missing result for any listed version.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-network comparison.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizer generalization under tuning.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and comparisons with other generalization measures.
Removing memorized examples and measuring test-accuracy effects.
